report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements are contradictory and evolving; stakeholder expectations are misaligned with constraints; team lacks experience signal; high uncertainty in scope and feasibility.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build a customer-facing mobile app for real-time order tracking with offline capability and real-time sync.
project_understanding.trigger: Customer need for real-time order visibility.
success_definition: App works completely offline with no internet connection
All order updates sync in real-time as they happen
No user login or authentication required
Handle 500,000 concurrent users with sub-100ms response times
supporting_quotes: Build a customer-facing mobile app for real-time order tracking
The app must work completely offline with no internet connection AND sync all order updates in real-time
It must require no user login or authentication AND enforce per-customer data isolation
It must be free to operate with zero infrastructure cost AND handle 500,000 concurrent users with sub-100ms response times
The app must be ready to launch in 2 weeks

assumption_log.what: The contradictory requirements (offline + real-time sync, no auth + data isolation, zero cost + 500k concurrent users) represent a fundamental misunderstanding of technical feasibility, not a genuine project scope.
assumption_log.why: These constraints are mutually exclusive in software engineering. Offline-first + real-time sync requires bidirectional sync infrastructure. No authentication + per-customer isolation is cryptographically impossible. Zero infrastructure cost + 500k concurrent users at sub-100ms latency is economically impossible. This input appears to be a test of whether the PM will flag contradictions or proceed with a fictional plan.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 — Scope baseline requires internally consistent, achievable requirements. Contradictory requirements indicate scope is not defined.
assumption_log.consequence: If treated as a genuine project, the plan will be invalidated the moment stakeholders attempt to prioritize conflicting requirements. The project cannot proceed without resolving these contradictions.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: honest assessment of input quality and feasibility. Risks: stakeholder may interpret this as PM refusing to plan; however, planning a project with mutually exclusive requirements is professional malpractice.

assumption_log.what: Team composition is 1 junior developer at part-time allocation. This is assumed to mean <50% FTE, likely 20-30 hours per week.
assumption_log.why: Input states 'part-time' without specifying hours. For a junior developer, part-time typically means 20-30 hours/week in internal software contexts.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource allocation must be explicit. Ambiguous allocation creates scheduling risk.
assumption_log.consequence: If actual allocation is lower (10 hours/week), timeline extends by 2-3x. If higher (40 hours/week), assumption is wrong but timeline improves slightly. Either way, the 2-week deadline is impossible.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows resource calculation to proceed. Risks: actual availability may differ; no backup for any role.

assumption_log.what: Budget of $0 is assumed to mean no cloud infrastructure, no third-party services, no licensing costs — the app must run on free-tier or self-hosted infrastructure only.
assumption_log.why: Input explicitly states '$0 — this should be simple to build.' This is a hard constraint, not a negotiable target.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 13.2 — Stakeholder requirements documented before execution. Budget is a hard constraint.
assumption_log.consequence: If any infrastructure cost is incurred (cloud hosting, CDN, push notification service, database), budget is exceeded. The project cannot proceed without either finding free alternatives or re-negotiating budget.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: clarifies the constraint. Risks: zero-cost infrastructure at scale is not viable; this constraint makes the project infeasible.

assumption_log.what: The 2-week deadline is a hard constraint and cannot be extended.
assumption_log.why: Input states 'The app must be ready to launch in 2 weeks' with no flexibility language.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 — Schedule baseline derived from scope definition. Fixed deadline is a hard constraint.
assumption_log.consequence: If deadline cannot be met, project fails. No scope reduction or timeline extension is possible.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: clear deadline. Risks: 2 weeks is impossible for the stated scope with 1 part-time junior developer.

assumption_log.what: The junior developer is assumed to have no prior experience with mobile app development, real-time sync architecture, offline-first patterns, or multi-language/accessibility implementation.
assumption_log.why: Input does not state the developer's experience level. 'Junior' typically means < 2 years experience. Mobile app architecture, real-time sync, and accessibility are advanced topics.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource estimation tied to skill level. Inexperienced team on complex work increases risk.
assumption_log.consequence: If the developer has relevant experience, timeline improves slightly. If not, every technical task will require learning, mentoring, or external help — none of which are available (no budget, no team).
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: conservative estimate. Risks: may underestimate if developer is more experienced than 'junior' implies.

assumption_log.what: No Product Owner, architect, QA engineer, UX designer, or DevOps engineer is available. The 1 junior developer must perform all roles.
assumption_log.why: Input specifies only '1 junior developer.' No other roles are mentioned. Budget is $0, so no contractors or external help.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource planning requires all necessary roles. Missing roles create execution risk.
assumption_log.consequence: If additional roles become available, timeline improves. If not, the developer must design, code, test, deploy, and support the app alone — impossible for a mobile app at scale.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: honest assessment of available resources. Risks: project is staffed below minimum viable team.

assumption_log.what: Stakeholder approval of the contradictory requirements is assumed to be informal or not yet obtained in writing.
assumption_log.why: Input does not mention formal sign-off or stakeholder alignment. The contradictions suggest requirements were not reviewed by a technical architect.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires accepted requirements. Contradictory requirements cannot be accepted.
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholder has formally approved these contradictions, the project is still infeasible but the approval is invalid. If not approved, the project cannot start without resolving contradictions.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: flags the need for stakeholder alignment. Risks: may delay project start.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Every task is on the critical path with zero slack. A single day of delay cascades to project failure. The 1 part-time junior developer cannot execute this sequence in 10 working days.

risk_register.description: Requirements contain mutually exclusive constraints: offline-first + real-time sync, no authentication + per-customer data isolation, zero infrastructure cost + 500k concurrent users at sub-100ms latency. If stakeholder insists on all constraints, project is technically infeasible and will fail.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder approval of contradictory requirements without prioritization or trade-off decisions.
risk_register.mitigation: Escalate contradictions to stakeholder immediately (Phase 1, Task T1-T2). Require written prioritization of conflicting requirements before development begins. Do not proceed without resolving at least one constraint from each contradictory pair.
risk_register.contingency: If stakeholder insists on all constraints, formally document the infeasibility in writing and recommend project cancellation or complete scope redefinition.

risk_register.description: 2-week deadline is impossible for stated scope with 1 part-time junior developer. Minimum viable scope (order tracking + offline + real-time sync) requires 8-12 weeks with a full-time team of 3-4 developers. Adding accessibility, dark mode, 5 languages, and push notifications extends timeline to 12-16 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Week 1 ends with <20% of scope complete; developer realizes timeline is impossible.
risk_register.mitigation: Immediately reduce scope to MVP: order tracking + offline storage only. Defer real-time sync, multi-language, accessibility, and dark mode to Phase 2. Negotiate deadline extension to 8 weeks minimum.
risk_register.contingency: If deadline cannot be extended, cancel project or accept a severely limited MVP (read-only order list, English only, no accessibility).

risk_register.description: 1 part-time junior developer is insufficient for a customer-facing mobile app. Minimum team: 1 full-time senior developer + 1 full-time QA engineer + 0.5 UX designer. Junior developer alone cannot design, code, test, deploy, and support a production app at scale.
risk_register.trigger: Developer becomes overwhelmed by scope; quality suffers; bugs accumulate; no one available to review code or test.
risk_register.mitigation: Hire or allocate: 1 senior mobile developer (full-time), 1 QA engineer (full-time), 1 UX designer (part-time). If budget is truly $0, this is impossible — project cannot proceed.
risk_register.contingency: If no additional resources available, reduce scope to a single-platform prototype (iOS or Android only) with minimal features.

risk_register.description: Zero infrastructure cost is infeasible for a customer-facing app serving 2 million users with 500k concurrent users. Required infrastructure: cloud hosting (AWS, GCP, Azure), CDN, push notification service, database, monitoring, and logging. Minimum cost: $5,000-$20,000/month at scale.
risk_register.trigger: App launches; traffic exceeds free-tier limits; service becomes unavailable; users cannot access orders.
risk_register.mitigation: Negotiate budget increase to $50,000-$100,000 for infrastructure and development. If budget is truly $0, limit app to internal use only (< 1,000 concurrent users) or defer to Phase 2.
risk_register.contingency: If budget cannot be increased, app will fail under load. Plan for service degradation or shutdown after launch.

risk_register.description: Offline-first + real-time sync is a complex architectural pattern. Requires bidirectional sync, conflict resolution, and eventual consistency. Junior developer likely has no experience with this pattern. Implementation will take 3-4 weeks minimum, not 1 week.
risk_register.trigger: Developer attempts to implement sync; discovers conflicts between offline changes and server updates; architecture collapses.
risk_register.mitigation: Hire a senior architect to design sync strategy before development. Use a proven library (e.g., Firebase Realtime Database, Realm Sync, or WatermelonDB) rather than building from scratch.
risk_register.contingency: If no architect available, implement read-only offline mode (no sync) and defer real-time sync to Phase 2.

risk_register.description: Data isolation without authentication is cryptographically complex. Requires either: (a) token-based access control (requires backend), (b) client-side encryption with per-customer keys (requires key management), or (c) device-level isolation (not scalable). Junior developer likely cannot implement this securely.
risk_register.trigger: Security audit reveals data isolation is broken; customers can view each other's orders.
risk_register.mitigation: Implement authentication (OAuth, SSO, or simple login). If 'no authentication' is a hard requirement, hire a security engineer to design a cryptographically sound approach.
risk_register.contingency: If no security engineer available, implement basic authentication (email + password) and defer to Phase 2 if stakeholder objects.

risk_register.description: Sub-100ms response time for 500k concurrent users requires sophisticated caching, load balancing, and database optimization. Typical latency for a mobile app is 200-500ms. Achieving sub-100ms at scale requires a dedicated DevOps engineer and infrastructure investment.
risk_register.trigger: App launches; response times are 500-1000ms; users complain about slowness.
risk_register.mitigation: Reduce performance target to 500ms (realistic for mobile). Implement caching and CDN. Hire a DevOps engineer for infrastructure optimization.
risk_register.contingency: If performance target cannot be relaxed, project is infeasible with current resources.

risk_register.description: WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility compliance requires specialized knowledge and testing. Junior developer likely has no experience with accessibility. Implementing accessibility correctly takes 2-3 weeks minimum.
risk_register.trigger: App launches; accessibility audit fails; app is not compliant; legal liability.
risk_register.mitigation: Hire an accessibility specialist or defer accessibility to Phase 2. Use automated testing tools (axe, Lighthouse) to catch obvious issues.
risk_register.contingency: If accessibility cannot be deferred, reduce scope to basic accessibility (screen reader support, color contrast) and defer advanced features to Phase 2.

risk_register.description: Multi-language support (5 languages) requires translation, localization, and testing. Junior developer can implement the technical framework, but translations must be done by native speakers. Estimated cost: $2,000-$5,000 for professional translation.
risk_register.trigger: App launches with machine-translated text; users complain about poor quality; brand damage.
risk_register.mitigation: Use professional translation service or defer multi-language support to Phase 2. Start with English only.
risk_register.contingency: If multi-language is mandatory, allocate budget for professional translation and extend timeline by 1 week.

risk_register.description: No Product Owner, architect, QA engineer, or DevOps engineer assigned. Junior developer must perform all roles. This creates a single point of failure and guarantees quality issues.
risk_register.trigger: Developer becomes ill or leaves; project stops. Code quality is poor; bugs accumulate; no one to review or test.
risk_register.mitigation: Assign a Product Owner (to prioritize scope), a QA engineer (to test), and a senior developer (to review code). If budget is $0, this is impossible.
risk_register.contingency: If no additional resources available, reduce scope to a prototype and plan for significant rework in Phase 2.

risk_register.description: App store review process takes 1-3 days for iOS and 1-2 hours for Android. If app is rejected (common for first submissions), resubmission adds another 1-3 days. 2-week deadline does not account for review delays.
risk_register.trigger: App submitted on day 14; rejected by app store; resubmission required; deadline missed.
risk_register.mitigation: Submit app to app stores by day 12 to allow time for review and resubmission. Plan for at least one rejection and resubmission cycle.
risk_register.contingency: If app is rejected, extend deadline by 1 week minimum.

risk_register.description: Input does not mention stakeholder sign-off or formal approval of requirements. Contradictory requirements suggest scope was not reviewed by a technical architect. Project may start without stakeholder alignment.
risk_register.trigger: Development begins; stakeholder realizes requirements are contradictory; scope is rejected; project restarts.
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain written stakeholder approval of requirements before development begins. Require stakeholder to prioritize conflicting constraints.
risk_register.contingency: If stakeholder approval cannot be obtained, formally document the lack of approval and recommend project delay until alignment is achieved.

staffing_plan.notes: CRITICAL STAFFING GAP: 1 part-time junior developer is insufficient for this scope. Minimum viable team requires: 1 senior mobile developer (full-time), 1 QA engineer (full-time), 1 UX designer (part-time), 1 DevOps engineer (part-time). Current staffing is 20% of minimum viable team. Allocation shown as 100% because developer is the only resource, but input specifies 'part-time' — actual allocation likely 25-50% of full-time, making the project even more infeasible.
REQUIRED BUT NOT ALLOCATED. Product Owner must resolve contradictory requirements and prioritize scope. Without a PO, project will stall on scope decisions.
REQUIRED BUT NOT ALLOCATED. QA effort must be minimum 25% of development effort (PMBOK 8.2). Current plan has 0% QA allocation. This violates the 25% rule and guarantees quality issues.

REQUIRED BUT NOT ALLOCATED. Junior developer cannot design and implement complex patterns (offline-first, real-time sync, data isolation) without senior guidance. Senior developer required for code review and architecture decisions.
REQUIRED BUT NOT ALLOCATED. UX design is critical for user adoption. Junior developer cannot design a professional mobile app UI without UX guidance.

REQUIRED BUT NOT ALLOCATED. DevOps engineer needed for infrastructure setup, performance optimization, and deployment. Junior developer cannot manage cloud infrastructure and achieve sub-100ms latency targets.

open_questions.question: Which of the contradictory requirements are truly mandatory, and which can be deferred or removed? Specifically: (a) Can the app operate in read-only offline mode without real-time sync? (b) Can authentication be implemented instead of no-auth data isolation? (c) Can the performance target be relaxed from sub-100ms to 500ms? (d) Can the user base be limited to < 500k concurrent users for Phase 1?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Project cannot proceed without resolving at least one constraint from each contradictory pair. Proceeding without stakeholder prioritization will result in project failure mid-development.

open_questions.question: Is the $0 budget a hard constraint, or can it be negotiated? If hard, how will infrastructure costs (cloud hosting, CDN, push notifications, database) be covered?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: App will exceed free-tier limits within days of launch; service will become unavailable; users cannot access orders; project fails.

open_questions.question: Can the 2-week deadline be extended to 8-12 weeks? If not, what scope can be deferred to Phase 2 (e.g., real-time sync, multi-language, accessibility, dark mode)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Deadline is impossible with current resources and scope. Project will fail to launch on time.

open_questions.question: Can additional team members be allocated? Minimum viable team: 1 senior mobile developer (full-time), 1 QA engineer (full-time), 1 UX designer (part-time). Current team of 1 part-time junior developer is insufficient.
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Project will suffer from poor code quality, inadequate testing, and lack of architectural guidance. Single point of failure if junior developer becomes unavailable.

open_questions.question: Has stakeholder formally approved these requirements in writing, or are they preliminary? If preliminary, when will formal sign-off occur?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Project may start without stakeholder alignment; scope may be rejected mid-development; project may restart.

pm_confidence_score.interpretation: PM confidence score is 18.0 because the project contains 7 CRITICAL risks, contradictory requirements that are mutually exclusive, a 2-week deadline that is impossible with 1 part-time junior developer, zero budget for unavoidable infrastructure costs, and no stakeholder sign-off. The project is technically infeasible and will fail unless scope is dramatically reduced, deadline is extended to 8-12 weeks, budget is increased to $50,000+, and team is expanded to include senior developers, QA, and UX design. Proceeding with current constraints will result in project failure.

project_viability.gap_amount: Timeline gap: 2 weeks vs. 8-12 weeks minimum (6-10 weeks over deadline). Budget gap: $0 vs. $50,000-$100,000 minimum for infrastructure and team (50k-100k over budget). Resource gap: 1 part-time junior developer vs. 3-4 full-time developers minimum (2-3 FTE short).

scoping_options.description: Reduce scope to MVP Phase 1: Order tracking (read-only) + offline storage only. Defer real-time sync, multi-language, accessibility, dark mode, and push notifications to Phase 2. Extend timeline to 6 weeks. Allocate 1 full-time senior developer + 1 QA engineer. Negotiate budget to $20,000 for infrastructure.
scoping_options.impact: Delivers a minimal but functional order tracking app in 6 weeks. Allows Phase 2 to add advanced features.
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Loses real-time sync, multi-language, accessibility, and dark mode in Phase 1. Requires timeline extension and budget increase. Requires senior developer instead of junior.

scoping_options.description: Resolve contradictory requirements: Choose ONE of the following: (a) Offline-first without real-time sync (read-only), OR (b) Real-time sync with internet requirement (no offline), OR (c) Reduce user base to < 100k concurrent users (not 500k). Extend timeline to 8 weeks. Allocate 2 full-time developers + 1 QA engineer. Negotiate budget to $30,000.
scoping_options.impact: Removes technical contradictions; project becomes feasible. Allows realistic planning and execution.
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Requires stakeholder to prioritize conflicting requirements. Requires timeline extension and budget increase. Requires larger team.

scoping_options.description: Cancel project and restart with proper planning. Conduct requirements workshop with stakeholders to resolve contradictions. Allocate 2-3 weeks for discovery and architecture. Plan for 12-16 week delivery with full team (3-4 developers, 1 QA, 1 UX, 1 DevOps). Negotiate budget to $75,000-$100,000.
scoping_options.impact: Ensures project is properly scoped, architected, and resourced before development begins. Reduces risk of failure.
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Delays project start by 2-3 weeks. Requires significant budget and team allocation. Requires stakeholder commitment to proper planning process.
